claims.text: The Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy is an additively manufactured dual-nanoprecipitation high-entropy alloy.
The additively manufactured alloy has enhanced strength relative to cast and wrought counterparts.
High-temperature oxidation induces preferential elemental redistribution at or near nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Elemental redistribution near nanoprecipitate interfaces governs the alloy's oxidation resistance.
Atom probe tomography can reveal oxidation-induced elemental redistribution at or near nanoprecipitate interfaces.
High-temperature oxidation drives elemental diffusion and segregation at nanoprecipitate boundaries.
APT provides atomic-scale resolution suitable for elucidating redistribution of Al, Ti, and Cr from nanoprecipitates or their interfaces.
Redistribution of Al, Ti, or Cr can alter local alloy chemistry.
Changes in local alloy chemistry caused by elemental redistribution can alter oxidation-barrier properties.
APT will detect significant post-oxidation changes in local composition near nanoprecipitate interfaces.
Post-oxidation interfacial composition changes may include enrichment of oxidation-prone or oxidation-resistant elements.
Elemental enrichment near nanoprecipitates will correlate with changes in oxide-scale formation.
The elemental redistribution is directly related to improved oxidation behavior.
Pre- and post-oxidation APT measurements can be compared to identify oxidation-induced changes in nanoprecipitate composition.
Cast or wrought alloy variants without the AM-induced precipitate structure can serve as production-route baselines.
Elemental redistribution is expected to matter specifically in high-temperature regimes where diffusion kinetics are significant.
Under milder oxidation conditions, elemental redistribution and its effect may be negligible.
